requirements.subject: ent:definition
requirements.canonical: A visible single definition MAY be imported by referring to its definition kind and its definition name(s).
requirements.original: Single visible definitions can be imported by referring to the definition kind and the definition name(s).

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of single definitions MAY be combined with imports of groups, imports of definitions of the same kind and imports of import statements.
requirements.original: The import of single definitions can be used in combination with imports of groups (see clause 8.2.3.3), with imports of definitions of the same kind (see clause 8.2.3.4), and with imports of import statements (see clause 8.2.3.7).

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement for single definitions has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleId "{" { ( type {TypeDefIdentifier [","]} | template {TemplateIdentifier [","]} | const {ConstIdentifier [","]} | testcase {TestcaseIdentifier [","]} | altstep {AltstepIdentifier [","]} | function {FunctionIdentifier [","]} | signature {SignatureIdentifier [","]} | modulepar {ModuleParIdentifier [","]} ) [";"] } "}" [";"].
requirements.original:
[ Visibility ] import from ModuleId "{" 
     {
       (
          ( type { TypeDefIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( template { TemplateIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( const { ConstIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( testcase { TestcaseIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( altstep { AltstepIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( function { FunctionIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( signature { SignatureIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( modulepar { ModuleParIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) 
       ) 
       [ ";" ] 
     }
  "}" [ ";" ]

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement that imports a definition which is not visible to the importing module SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Import of an invisible definition shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:definition
requirements.canonical: A single definition to be imported SHALL be defined in the module from which it is imported.
requirements.original: a) The definition to be imported shall be defined in the module from which it is to be imported and shall be visible to the importing module.

requirements.subject: ent:definition
requirements.canonical: A single definition to be imported SHALL be visible to the importing module.
requirements.original: a) The definition to be imported shall be defined in the module from which it is to be imported and shall be visible to the importing module.

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: A group of definitions MAY be imported.
requirements.original: Groups of definitions may be imported.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of groups MAY be combined with imports of single definitions, imports of definitions of the same kind and imports of import statements.
requirements.original: The import of groups can be used in combination with imports of single definitions (see clause 8.2.3.2), with imports of definitions of the same kind (see clause 8.2.3.4), and with imports of import statements (see clause 8.2.3.7).

requirements.subject: ent:sub-group
requirements.canonical: A sub-group MAY be imported directly, without importing the groups in which the sub-group is embedded.
requirements.original: It is allowed to import sub-groups (i.e. a group which is defined within another group) directly, i.e. without the groups in which the sub-group is embedded.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.condition: the name of the sub-group to be imported is identical to the name of another sub-group in the same module
requirements.canonical: If the name of a sub-group to be imported is identical to the name of another sub-group in the same module, the import statement SHALL use the dot notation to identify the sub-group uniquely.
requirements.original: If the name of a sub-group that should be imported is identical to the name of another sub-group in the same module (see clause 8.2.2), the dot notation shall be used to identify the sub-group to be imported uniquely.

requirements.subject: ent:except-specification
requirements.condition: some visible definitions of the group are not to be imported
requirements.canonical: If visible definitions of an imported group are not to be imported, their kinds and identifiers SHALL be listed in the exception list enclosed in curly brackets following the `except` keyword.
requirements.original: If some visible definitions of a group are wished not to be imported, their kinds and identifiers shall be listed in the exception list within a pair of curly brackets following the except keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword MAY be used in the exception list of a group import.
requirements.original: The all keyword is also allowed to be used in the exception list; this will exclude all definitions of the same kind from the import statement.

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword used for a definition kind in the exception list of a group import excludes all definitions of that kind of the group from the import statement.
requirements.original: The all keyword is also allowed to be used in the exception list; this will exclude all definitions of the same kind from the import statement.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement for groups has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleId "{" { ( group { QualifiedIdentifier [ except "{" ExceptSpec "}" ] [","] } ) [";"] } "}" [";"].

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: Importing a group IS equivalent to an import statement that lists all visible definitions of the group, including its sub-groups, except those listed in the except specification.
requirements.original: The effect of importing a group is identical to an import statement that lists all visible definitions (including sub-groups) of this group except of those that are listed in the except specification.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: Import statements contained in an imported group or in its sub-groups ARE NOT part of the group import; only definitions are imported.
requirements.original: Import statements contained in the group or in its subgroups are not part of this list, only definitions are.

requirements.subject: ent:except-specification
requirements.canonical: An except specification of an import statement IS NOT an exclusion of the listed definitions from being imported by other imports.
requirements.original: It is important to point out, that the except statement does not exclude the definitions listed from being imported in general; all statements importing definitions of the same kind can be seen as a shorthand notation for an equivalent list of identifiers of single definitions.

ambiguity.issue: 'except statement' is used for the except specification, which is not a statement.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of all definitions of the same kind IS a shorthand notation for an equivalent list of identifiers of single definitions.
requirements.original: It is important to point out, that the except statement does not exclude the definitions listed from being imported in general; all statements importing definitions of the same kind can be seen as a shorthand notation for an equivalent list of identifiers of single definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:except-specification
requirements.canonical: An except specification excludes definitions only from the single list of definitions of the import to which it belongs.
requirements.original: The except statement excludes definitions from this single list only.

ambiguity.issue: 'except statement' is used for the except specification, which is not a statement.

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: A group to be imported SHALL be defined in the module from which it is imported.
requirements.original: a) The group to be imported shall be defined in the module from which it is to be imported.

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword MAY be used to import all visible definitions of the same kind of a module.
requirements.original: The all keyword may be used to import all visible definitions of the same kind of a module.

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword used with the `const` keyword identifies all visible constants declared in the module definitions part of the module referenced by the import statement.
requirements.original: The all keyword used with the constant keyword identifies all visible constants declared in the definitions part of the module the import statement refers to.

ambiguity.issue: 'constant keyword' is used, the TTCN-3 keyword is `const`.

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword used with the `function` keyword identifies all visible functions, all visible external functions and the visible module control part of the module referenced by the import statement.
requirements.original: Similarly the all keyword used with the function keyword identifies all visible functions, all visible external functions defined and the visible module control function in the module the import statement denotes.

ambiguity.issue: 'module control function' is used for the module control part, which is not a function elsewhere in the standard.

requirements.subject: ent:except-specification
requirements.condition: some visible declarations of the kind are to be excluded
requirements.canonical: If visible definitions of a kind are to be excluded from an import of all definitions of that kind, their identifiers SHALL be listed following the `except` keyword.
requirements.original: If some visible declarations of a kind are wished to be excluded from the given import statement, their identifiers shall be listed following the except keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of definitions of the same kind MAY be combined with imports of single definitions, imports of groups and imports of import statements.
requirements.original: The import of visible definitions of the same kind can be used in combination with imports of single visible definitions (see clause 8.2.3.2), with imports of groups (see clause 8.2.3.3), and with imports of import statements (see clause 8.2.3.7).

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement for definitions of the same kind has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleId "{" { ( Kind all [ except { Identifier [","] } ] ) [";"] } "}" [";"], where Kind is one of type, template, const, testcase, altstep, function, signature or modulepar.
requirements.original:
[ Visibility ] import from ModuleId "{" 
     {
       (
          ( type all [ except { TypeDefIdentifier [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( template all [ except { TemplateIdentifier  [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( const all [ except { ConstIdentifier  [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( testcase all [ except { TestcaseIdentifier  [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( altstep all [ except { AltstepIdentifier  [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( function all [ except { FunctionIdentifier  [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( signature all [ except { SignatureIdentifier [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( modulepar all [ except { ModuleParIdentifier [ "," ] } ] )
       ) 
       [ ";" ] 
     }
  "}" [ ";" ]

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: Importing definitions of the same kind IS equivalent to an import statement that lists all visible definitions of that kind except those listed in the except specification.
requirements.original: The effect of importing definitions of the same kind is identical to an import statement that lists all visible definitions of that kind except of those that are listed in the except specification.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.condition: the resulting list of definitions is empty
requirements.canonical: An import of definitions of the same kind whose resulting list of visible definitions, after removing the excepted ones, is empty has no effect.
requirements.original: NOTE: If the list of all visible definitions of that kind except of those that are listed in the except specification is empty, the import statement has no effect.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of definitions of the same kind whose resulting list of definitions is empty DOES NOT cause an error.
requirements.original: This case does not lead to an error.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement MAY import all visible definitions of the module definitions part of a module by using the `all` keyword next to the module name.
requirements.original: All visible definitions of a module definitions part may be imported using the all keyword next to the module name.

requirements.subject: ent:except-specification
requirements.condition: some visible definitions are not to be imported
requirements.canonical: If visible definitions are not to be imported by an import of all definitions of a module, their kinds and identifiers SHALL be listed in the exception list enclosed in curly brackets following the `except` keyword.
requirements.original: If some visible definitions are wished not to be imported, their kinds and identifiers shall be listed in the exception list within a pair of curly brackets following the except keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword MAY be used in the exception list of an import of all definitions of a module.
requirements.original: The all keyword is also allowed to be used in the exception list; this will exclude all visible declarations of the same kind from the import statement.

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword used for a definition kind in the exception list of an import of all definitions excludes all visible declarations of that kind from the import statement.
requirements.original: The all keyword is also allowed to be used in the exception list; this will exclude all visible declarations of the same kind from the import statement.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.condition: the resulting list of definitions is empty
requirements.canonical: An import of all definitions of a module whose resulting list of visible definitions, after removing the excepted ones, is empty has no effect.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: If the list of all visible definitions of a module except of those that are listed in the except specification is empty, the import statement has no effect.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of all definitions of a module whose resulting list of definitions is empty DOES NOT cause an error.
requirements.original: This case does not lead to an error.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of all definitions of a module imports only the definitions declared directly in that module, including the address type and the module control part if they are specified.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Importing all definitions of a module imports only definitions declared directly in that module including the address type and module control function (if they are specified), but does not import the import statements of that module (see also clause 8.2.3.7).

ambiguity.issue: 'module control function' is used for the module control part.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of all definitions of a module DOES NOT import the import statements of that module.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Importing all definitions of a module imports only definitions declared directly in that module including the address type and module control function (if they are specified), but does not import the import statements of that module (see also clause 8.2.3.7).

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement for all definitions of a module has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleId all [ { except "{" ( Kind { Identifier [","] } | all ) ... "}" [";"] } ] [";"], where Kind is one of group, type, template, const, testcase, altstep, function, signature or modulepar.
requirements.original:
[ Visibility ] import from ModuleId
     all
     [ 
       {
          except "{"
            ( group { QualifiedIdentifier [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( type { TypeDefIdentifier [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( template { TemplateIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( const { ConstIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( testcase { TestcaseIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( altstep { AltstepIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( function { FunctionIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( signature { SignatureIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( modulepar { ModuleParIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) 
          "}" 
          [ ";" ] 
       }
     ]
  [ ";" ]

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: Importing all visible definitions of a module IS equivalent to an import statement that lists all importable definitions of that module except those listed in the except specification.
requirements.original: The effect of importing all visible definitions of a module is identical to an import statement that lists all importable definitions of that module except of those that are listed in the except specification.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.condition: all visible definitions of a module are imported with the `all` keyword
requirements.canonical: An import statement that imports all visible definitions of a module with the `all` keyword SHALL NOT contain any other form of import (import of single definitions, import of definitions of the same kind, etc.).
requirements.original: a) If all visible definitions of a module are imported by using the all keyword, no other form of import (import of single definitions, import of the same kind, etc.) shall be used for the same import statement.

requirements.subject: ent:except-specification
requirements.canonical: The except specification of an import of all definitions SHALL contain at most one except entry per kind of definition (group, type, etc.).
requirements.original: b) In the set of except statements for an all import, only one except statement per kind of definition (i.e. for a group, type, etc.) is allowed.

ambiguity.issue: 'except statement' is used for the per-kind entries of the except specification.
